title: The 3-2-1 backup rule: why one copy is never enough

narration: Say your report is due tomorrow.
It lives in one place: your laptop.
beats.visual_intent: One file object labelled Report sits inside a single laptop on the plain light field; nothing else exists yet.

grounding.claim: a report kept only on a laptop

narration: Tonight, the drive dies.
The report goes with it.
beats.visual_intent: The laptop's drive fails; the report fades to an empty outline and nothing on the field can bring it back.

grounding.claim: losing the only copy means the data is gone
hardware failure is a cause of data loss

narration: One copy is a single point of failure.
The fix is three numbers.
beats.visual_intent: The empty outline is labelled single point of failure, then 3-2-1 is set large beside it.

grounding.claim: a single copy is a single point of failure
the rule is 3-2-1

narration: A dead drive is one way to lose it.
A stolen laptop.
A wrong delete.
Ransomware.
beats.visual_intent: Four failures arrive one at a time around the single report, each a small labelled mark that lands on its word and empties the file.

grounding.claim: hardware failure, a lost or stolen device, accidental deletion and ransomware cause data loss

narration: Start with three: the original, plus two backups.
One failure no longer leaves you with zero.
beats.visual_intent: The report copies twice into three files in a row; one is struck and two remain. The 3 lights.

grounding.claim: three copies of data
the original plus two backups

narration: Two: two kinds of storage.
Say, the laptop and an external drive.
One fault is unlikely to take both.
beats.visual_intent: A copy moves from the laptop to an external drive; a fault strikes the laptop only and the drive's copy stays whole. The 2 lights.

grounding.claim: two different types of storage
different storage types fail in different ways, so one fault is unlikely to remove every copy

narration: But both sit on your desk.
One fire, flood or theft takes them together.
beats.visual_intent: A boundary draws round the desk holding laptop and drive; one event fills the whole boundary and both copies go together.
beats.misconception: a second copy in the same place is safe

grounding.claim: copies in the same place can be lost together by one event such as theft, fire or flood

narration: So, one: keep a copy offsite.
The cloud is a common way to do it.
beats.visual_intent: A copy travels out of the boundary to a cloud far across the field, out of the event's reach. The 1 lights.

grounding.claim: one copy offsite
an offsite copy is in a different location, so an event there does not reach it
cloud storage is a common way to keep the offsite copy

narration: Ransomware can encrypt backups that stay connected.
So keep one offline or disconnected.
beats.visual_intent: A lock spreads along a connected line into one backup; the disconnected copy, with no line to it, stays clean.

grounding.claim: ransomware can encrypt connected backups; guidance advises keeping one offline or disconnected

narration: Not more copies.
Copies that cannot all fail together.
beats.visual_intent: The whole system at rest: laptop, external drive and cloud, each holding its copy, with 3, 2 and 1 lit beside them.
beats.misconception: more copies is what makes data safe

grounding.claim: the 3-2-1 rule
copies that can fail together add little

narration: Quick check.
A laptop and a USB backup, in the same bag.
Which part breaks?
beats.visual_intent: A bag outline holds a laptop and a USB drive, each with a copy of the report; 3, 2 and 1 sit below, unlit, waiting.

grounding.claim: a laptop and USB drive in the same bag
the rule's three parts

narration: The one.
They travel together, so one stolen bag takes both.
beats.visual_intent: 3 and 2 light, 1 stays dark and is marked missing; then the bag leaves the field with both copies inside.

grounding.claim: copies in the same place can be lost together by one theft
offsite means a different location

narration: Same night, same failure.
This time the report opens from a backup.
beats.visual_intent: The opening laptop fails again exactly as before; the report comes back from the external drive while the cloud copy stays whole.

grounding.claim: the same failure replayed with backups in place
copies elsewhere survive a failure of the laptop

narration: Now check your own key files.
Which number is missing?
beats.visual_intent: Three file objects, each beside the 3-2-1 marks, waiting to be checked off: the viewer's own task.

grounding.claim: the 3-2-1 rule as a check
